lines.text: The birth of a baby.
Most women give birth [bevallen] in the hospital.
Were there problems during the pregnancy [zwangerschap]?
Then you are monitored by the gynaecologist [gynaecoloog] in the hospital, who is then also present at the birth.
No problems?
Then you can give birth with the help of a midwife [verloskundige].
That can be in the hospital, but also at home.
You must get all the baby supplies yourself.
If you are pregnant, you must also arrange a maternity home-care nurse [kraamhulp] yourself in time.
The kraamhulp comes to help at your home for about a week after the baby is born.
The health insurance [zorgverzekering] does not always cover all the costs; sometimes there is a personal contribution [eigen bijdrage].
The child health clinic [consultatiebureau] is part of the GGD (Gemeentelijke Gezondheidsdienst) in the municipality where you live.
Doctors and nurses [verpleegkundigen] work there.
You can go there with your child from zero to four years old.
They check whether your child is healthy: they measure [meten] and weigh [wegen] your child, and they look at the development [ontwikkeling] — seeing, hearing, talking, playing, eating, sleeping.
Your child can get vaccinations [vaccinaties] there against diseases.
The consultatiebureau is free [gratis].
Responsible for your child.
Parents are responsible for their children.
If a child does not come to school, the parents can get a fine [boete].
Until a child is sixteen, the parents are also liable [aansprakelijk]: if a child breaks something on the street, the parents must pay for it.
Help with parenting.
Is your child younger than four?
Then you can talk about problems at the consultatiebureau.
Is the child four or older?
Then you can talk at school.
You can also always talk with the family doctor [huisarts].
Do the problems continue?
Then you can get help from the municipality, for example youth care [jeugdzorg].
They do research and give advice, often also in your own language.
Not safe.
Sometimes parents abuse [mishandelen] their child, or they can no longer take care of the child.
Then the Child Protection Board [Raad voor de Kinderbescherming] can do something.
Only if the situation is very serious can the judge [rechter] make a decision, for example that the child no longer lives with the parents.
Are you worried about the safety of a child (including someone else's child)?
Then you can call Veilig Thuis for advice.
Abuse of children.
Children have rights [rechten], for example the right to education.
Abuse is forbidden [verboden].
Hitting children is not allowed: not by teachers and not by parents either.
Circumcision [Besnijdenis] of girls is forbidden in the Netherlands.
Circumcision of boys is not forbidden.
